dependance.r1_d: You love without losing yourself. Your partner is a choice, not a life raft: you have a life, friends and projects of your own, and the relationship adds to them instead of replacing everything. Silences don't frighten you, disagreements don't threaten you.
dependance.r1_a: Keep that balance alive: it rests on everything you keep nurturing outside the couple. And if your partner shows signs of dependency, your steadiness will be precious for talking about it without judgement.
dependance.r2_d: Your attachment is strong and comes with a few anxious reflexes: a need for reassurance here, an evening ruined by a silence there. Nothing entrenched, but you probably recognised some situations in this test a little too well.
dependance.r2_a: Spot the trigger that comes back most often (silence, distance, conflict) and work on that one first. This is the right moment: anxious habits are far easier to correct before they become a way of functioning.
dependance.r3_d: The relationship occupies a place you no longer really control: your mood depends on theirs, your decisions wait for their approval, your friends and projects have faded into the background. This is not a character flaw, it's a mechanism, and it has a history.
dependance.r3_a: Start by reclaiming territory of your own: an activity, friends, a project that belongs only to you. Not against your couple, but for you. If the anxiety resists, psychological support often saves years.
dependance.r4_t: Strong dependency, and it's hurting you
dependance.r4_d: Your answers describe real suffering: physical anxiety in their absence, your needs erased, fear of abandonment dictating your choices. You're no longer living the relationship, you're clinging to it. And you deserve better than this permanent fear.
dependance.r4_a: Talk to a professional, a psychologist or therapist: emotional dependency responds very well to treatment, and nobody should go through it alone. In the meantime, one concrete first step: this week, reach out to someone you've lost touch with.
dependance.q1: Your partner hasn't replied for three hours, and they're simply at work.
dependance.q1a: It doesn't even cross your mind. You both have your own days.
dependance.q1b: You notice it, but it changes nothing about your afternoon.
dependance.q1c: You reread your last message to check you didn't write anything wrong.
dependance.q1d: You pace around, send another message, and the anxiety climbs with every silent minute.
dependance.q2: Friends invite you on a weekend away, without your partner.
dependance.q2a: You accept gladly. It does you good too.
dependance.q2b: You accept, knowing you'll miss your partner a little.
dependance.q2c: You hesitate for a long time: leaving without them makes you uneasy.
dependance.q2d: You decline. A weekend away from them isn't a break, it's an ordeal.
dependance.q3: Finish this sentence honestly: “Without this relationship, I would be...”
dependance.q3a: Sad for a while, then myself again.
dependance.q3b: Lost for some time, but I know I'd recover.
dependance.q3c: Missing a part of who I've become.
dependance.q3d: I honestly don't know. I can no longer define myself without them.
dependance.q4: You disagree about something that matters to you. The discussion heats up.
dependance.q4a: You stand your ground, even if there's friction for a while.
dependance.q4b: You look for a compromise, even if it means giving up some ground.
dependance.q4c: You often give in: the disagreement costs you more than being right is worth.
dependance.q4d: You almost always capitulate. A conflict feels like a risk of losing them.
dependance.q5: “Do you love me?” How often does this question, or some version of it, leave your mouth?
dependance.q5a: Rarely. You don't feel the need.
dependance.q5b: From time to time, in tender moments.
dependance.q5c: Often, and the answer soothes you... for an hour or two.
dependance.q5d: Almost every day, and no answer ever really feels like enough.
dependance.q6: The friends you had before the relationship: how often do you see them?
dependance.q6a: As much as before. Your social life hasn't moved.
dependance.q6b: A little less, like in any new couple.
dependance.q6c: Far less, and you've let friendships that mattered slip away.
dependance.q6d: Almost never. Your world has shrunk to your couple without you ever deciding it.
dependance.q7: Your partner laughs at a message and doesn't tell you who it's from.
dependance.q7a: You pay no attention to it.
dependance.q7b: You ask out of curiosity, nothing more.
dependance.q7c: It nags at you for part of the evening.
dependance.q7d: You don't let it go until you know, and you'd check their phone if you could.
dependance.q8: Expressing a need that might not go down well, like “I'd like us to change this”...
dependance.q8a: You just do it. That's what a couple is for.
dependance.q8b: You do it, picking the right moment.
dependance.q8c: You circle around it for weeks before daring to say it.
dependance.q8d: You don't dare. Asking means risking disappointment, and disappointing means risking losing them.
dependance.q9: Be honest: a relationship that hurts you, but a relationship all the same, or no relationship at all?
dependance.q9a: No relationship at all. Being alone doesn't destroy you.
dependance.q9b: The question is uncomfortable, but loneliness doesn't scare you enough to accept anything.
dependance.q9c: You've already stayed too long in a relationship that was damaging you, and you know it.
dependance.q9d: A relationship, even a painful one. The void is worse than anything.
dependance.q10: Imagine for ten seconds that your partner leaves you tomorrow. What dominates?
dependance.q10a: Sadness. A breakup is always a loss.
dependance.q10b: Sadness and real worry, for as long as it takes to absorb it.
dependance.q10c: A fear that grips your throat at the mere thought.
dependance.q10d: Almost physical panic. You avoid even imagining that scenario.
dependance.q11: Booking a restaurant, picking a film, changing your haircut: deciding alone...
dependance.q11a: No problem at all. You don't need approval.
dependance.q11b: You like having their opinion, but you decide without them.
dependance.q11c: You ask almost every time, “just to be sure”.
dependance.q11d: Deciding without them feels unthinkable, even for trivial things.
dependance.q12: Your partner comes home in a bad mood, for a reason that has nothing to do with you.
dependance.q12a: You sympathise, but their mood remains theirs.
dependance.q12b: It affects you. You try to help them decompress.
dependance.q12c: Their mood contaminates yours: no good evening is possible if they're doing badly.
dependance.q12d: You feel responsible and bend over backwards to fix it, as if it were your fault.
dependance.q13: They leave for a week-long work trip.
dependance.q13a: The week flies by. You have your own life.
dependance.q13b: You miss them, especially in the evenings.
dependance.q13c: You count the days and the home feels empty.
dependance.q13d: You sleep badly, eat badly, and run on empty until they're back.
dependance.q14: Since this relationship began, your personal projects (studies, work, passions)...
dependance.q14a: Move forward as before. Your couple adds to them.
dependance.q14b: Have slowed a little. Time gets shared.
dependance.q14c: Are on standby: you organise everything around the relationship.
dependance.q14d: Have disappeared. You'd struggle to name one project that doesn't include your partner.
dependance.q15: Between two relationships, in your life, there usually passes...
dependance.q15a: However long it takes. You know how to live alone.
dependance.q15b: A few months, with no particular urgency.
dependance.q15c: Very little: you cope badly with periods alone.
dependance.q15d: Almost nothing. You chain them, sometimes starting the next before the last has ended.
dependance.q16: Your sense of your own worth comes mostly from...
dependance.q16a: What you think of yourself, even if their view matters.
dependance.q16b: A mix of your view and theirs, like everyone.
dependance.q16c: Largely from their compliments and reproaches: one wrong word wrecks your day.
dependance.q16d: Entirely from their eyes. If they doubt you, you're worth nothing.
dependance.q17: When your partner pulls back (a silent evening, a colder tone)...
dependance.q17a: You give them space. It happens to everyone.
dependance.q17b: You ask if they're okay, then respect their silence.
dependance.q17c: You need to close the gap immediately, with messages and attention.
dependance.q17d: Your body reacts: knotted stomach, short breath, unable to think of anything else.
dependance.q18: Have you ever provoked an argument or a crisis “to see” if they cared about you?
dependance.q18a: Never. The idea hasn't even crossed your mind.
dependance.q18b: Maybe once, without putting it in those words.
dependance.q18d: It's a recurring pattern: testing their love has become your way of reassuring yourself.
dependance.q19: Accepting things that go against your values, for them...
dependance.q19a: No. Your limits are clear and they know them.
dependance.q19b: You've made compromises, but nothing that betrays who you are.
dependance.q19c: You've already said yes to things that bothered you, to avoid making waves.
dependance.q19d: You've given up limits that mattered, because holding them might have driven them away.
dependance.q20: An evening alone at home, nothing special going on: what do you feel?
dependance.q20a: Calm. Those evenings do you good.
dependance.q20c: A diffuse emptiness you fill however you can: screens, fridge, endless scrolling.
dependance.q20d: A dull, almost physical anxiety, as if something were missing inside.
